english.title: Fail to comply with requirements of notice to chief officer of a shotgun transaction
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), failed to comply with section 42A(2) of the Firearms Act 1968 in that the notice of transaction sent by you to the chief officer of police for **(..SPECIFY CHIEF OFFICER..) under section 42A(1) of the Firearms Act 1968 did not contain a description of the shotgun, state the nature of the transaction and set out the particulars of any licence granted for the purposes of an order made under section 1 of the Import, Export and Customs Powers (Defence) Act 1939 by virtue of which the transaction was authorised under section 17 of the Firearms (Amendment) Act 1988
english.legislation: Contrary to section 42A(3) of and Schedule 6 to the Firearms Act 1968.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
failed to comply with section 42A(2) Firearms Act
in that a notice of transaction sent to chief officer of police
did not contain description of shotgun
state nature of transaction
set out particulars of relevant licence

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Three months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five.

Time limit for prosecutions:
4 years

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
